newsitem.title: USA: UNITED HEALTHCARE CITES LAGGING MARGINS.
newsitem.headline: UNITED HEALTHCARE CITES LAGGING MARGINS.

text.p: United HealthCare Corp said Thursday lagging margins in several markets had restrained earnings growth in the second quarter and were likely to be "a drag on earnings for the remainder of 1997."
The company did manage, however, to match the First Call consensus analysts' earnings estimate of $0.57 per share for the second quarter, versus $0.23 per share seen in the 1996 quarter.
The company said, excluding non-recurring charges in the 1996 quarter, its 1997 second quarter earnings rose 33 percent to $0.43 per share.
It said year-on-year revenues for the 1997 second quarter ended June 30 rose 18 percent to $2.9 billion.
The company said net earnings reached $116 million in the second quarter. That compares with $87 million in the 1996 quarter, excluding non-recurring charges.
"We are, of course, pleased with the progress made during the second quarter," said chief executive William McGuire.

"However, we are now focusing significant resources to ensure improved performance in a few health plan markets, most notably Maryland, Rhode Island, and the Gulf Coast, in which we have not yet reached margins achieved in aggregate by our other health plans," he added.
"Achieving comparable margins to those in our other markets could have contributed an additional $0.06 per share in earnings in the second quarter," McGuire said.
"While improved performance is expected in these markets, the performance at these health plans will continue to be a drag on earnings for the remainder of 1997," he said.

The company said its overall medical care ratio in the second quarter rose 30 basis points to 84.7 percent from the previous quarter. The ratio is a measure of the portion of premium revenues paid out to cover medical costs of members.

The company said factors contributing to the higher ratio in the recent quarter included higher seasonal use of health care services encountered during the first half of any year and continued investment in new Medicare markets.
But it said the ratio fell 10 basis points from the 84.8 percent reported in the second quarter of 1996, excluding non-recurring charges last year.
Same-store Medicare enrollment was up 55 percent from the previous year, with total Medicare enrollment ending the quarter at 286,000, the company said.
